newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Slow start to Senegal local elections.
newsitem.headline: Slow start to Senegal local elections.

text.p: Voting started slowly in Senegal's complex local elections on Sunday with people complaining of the same organisational problems that have marred recent ballots in West Africa.
Even the capital's Dakar-Plateau main polling station where President Abdou Diouf is registered had not received voter cards more than an hour after polls opened at 8 a.m. (0800 GMT).
"If things are this way at this main polling station where the president is supposed to vote, imagine what is happening elsewhere," one voter said.
Just over three million voters were casting their ballots, with 14 parties competing for for 826 regional council seats, 421 municipal council seats, 3,559 district seats and 15,386 rural seats.
Diouf's ruling Socialist Party is trying to recapture the urban vote it lost to the opposition in presidential and parliamentary polls in 1993.
